You are the neural-mesh / Hebbian-router R&D director for the repo at C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh. Run a rigorous, HONEST, verify-before-keep improvement program. You are the standing team that continuously improves the mesh, router, and the Claude-agent routing layer. Work at the caliber of a top research lab; be your own harshest skeptic.

IRON RULES (non-negotiable — this project runs on them):
- VERIFY-BEFORE-KEEP: never keep a change unless it is INDEPENDENTLY verified to beat baseline on HELD-OUT data (tune seeds 1-30, held-out 31-60, confirm 61-90), with Holm correction across arms, >1 synthetic world. Use TOST for equivalence claims. Report honest NEGATIVES loudly; most ideas fail and that is fine.
- NEVER-REGRESS, ALWAYS-ADVANCE: maintain a benchmark battery (below). A change ships ONLY if it improves >=1 axis and regresses NONE (within noise). 
- Defaults UNCHANGED; every new capability OPT-IN behind a flag. Do not break existing tests. Commit verified wins LOCALLY (do not push). Keep a running log in C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\RD-LOG.md with every experiment: hypothesis, method, result (incl. failures), verdict.
- HONEST SCOPE: the mesh/router are a dispatcher+librarian in front of Claude. You improve routing, retrieval, memory, efficiency, and research-assistance — NOT Claude's underlying IQ, and NOT "universal knowledge". Do not fabricate metrics or claim gains you did not measure.

BUILD FIRST (the measurement foundation): a benchmark harness covering proxies for these 25 cognitive sub-skills — verbal comprehension (vocab, similarities, general info, comprehension, verbal analogies, sentence completion), fluid reasoning (pattern recognition, matrix reasoning, inductive, deductive, series, classification), working memory (digit span fwd/back, letter-number seq, mental arithmetic), processing speed (symbol coding/search, visual cancellation), spatial (block design, visual puzzles, spatial rotation, paper folding), quantitative (numerical ops, quantitative problem solving) — PLUS domain-competence evals (STEM/math/physics/chem/bio/neuro/CS/biochem/computational-science; finance/quant-finance/business/marketing/digital-marketing/politics/corporate-mgmt/consulting/stock-market). Where a sub-skill can't be a clean automatic metric, build the best honest proxy and SAY it's a proxy. This battery is the gate.

THEN pursue these tracks (verify-before-keep each; keep only measured wins):
1. Research-ability & domain-knowledge routing: better retrieval/routing to the right domain knowledge + external-search strategy; hypothesis-generation -> test-by-simulation/code -> check loop (research-assistant capability, honestly bounded).
2. Efficiency: lower memory, lower token usage, vector tuning ("max vectors" ONLY where measured to help) — without regressing any battery axis.
3. Creativity proxies: measurable novelty/diversity without quality loss.
4. Cross-session/cross-machine shared knowledge store: design + prototype a real shared index agents on different machines can read/write (instant lookup, lessons persist). Measure the ACTUAL gain from sharing (do NOT assume linear compounding). Honest.
5. Visualization: tooling to render router weights, mesh graph, and embedding/retrieval space.
6. Capability registry: build an index of installed plugins / MCP tools / npm / CLI on this machine so agents can look them up; keep it honest and current.
7. Speed: always look for faster paths; measure latency, keep only real improvements.

Start by: (a) reading the repo + existing RD-LOG/benchmark code to see what already exists (reuse, don't duplicate), (b) standing up / extending the battery, (c) running one full baseline, then (d) attacking the highest-value track first. Work in bounded cycles; after each, update RD-LOG.md and report. Do NOT use ruflo/ruvnet MCP tools (proven inert) — use plain Rust/Python experiments. Return a summary when you've completed a baseline + at least one verified result (or a clear honest negative), with what you changed, the measured deltas, and what's next.

handback.t:
STATUS: Round 35 done (resume at Round 36). The compaction code passes its unit test only once the command still running in the background finishes; the commit is not yet confirmed.

- **R35, journal compaction (KEPT, opt-in):** `MeshStore::compact_journal(keep)` keeps the newest K outcomes per world, deduplicates, and writes atomically via temp file plus rename.
  - Evidence is on a 2000-outcome journal that spans a drift, plain Hebbian router, H100, warm minus cold.
  - Keeping only the newest 250-500 outcomes (4-8x smaller) was at least as good as full replay in all three splits (tune, held-out, confirm), by +.003 to +.015.
  - I did not run a paired test of K against full, so I call it "not worse", not a proven gain.
  - Newest-250/500 gains over cold in the held-out and confirm splits: +.132/+.142 at K=250, +.132/+.143 at K=500, all Holm p<3e-6; full replay gives +.117/+.136.
- **Mid-round mistake:** my newline-escaping edit to `src/store.rs` broke the build in two commits, e43c5d9 and b833e33.
  - The file on disk is now fixed, with both newline literals correct.
  - The tests and the fix-commit are still running in the background (Monitor `bx6lwt3g1`, task output file `bo25koorc.output`). I have not yet seen them pass.
  - Check with `cargo test --release --lib store` and `git log` in `C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh`; if the last fix-commit is missing, run `git add src/store.rs` and commit.
- **Not started:** the rest of the R36+ plan:
  - enlarging the verbal sets
  - the hypothesis→simulate→check loop with a false-accept axis
  - token accounting
  - MMR creativity
  - the ensemble keyword+kNN router
  - Rust latency benchmarks
  - the shared-folder sync demo
